title: Implement A/B Model Testing Framework in BizSight Inference Dashboard
description: The BizSight Inference Dashboard is a C-based command-line tool for running and monitoring ML model inference pipelines. Currently, it supports evaluating only one model at a time. The objective is to extend its functionality to support A/B testing, allowing a 'champion' model to be compared against a 'challenger' model on the same dataset. This is a complex task requiring incremental development and a deep understanding of the existing architecture, from data structures and model execution to monitoring and viewmodel logic.

project_spec.name: BizSight Inference Dashboard
project_spec.description:
BizSight Inference Dashboard is an entry-level yet fully-structured ML-inference toolkit targeted at small and mid-sized companies that want to embed predictive insights into existing C-based back-office software (pricing engines, inventory trackers, POS terminals). Built on a strict MVVM separation, the project demonstrates how a lightweight C codebase can expose business-ready forecasts while remaining maintainable and testable.

Within the Model layer, a factory builds concrete inference engines (e.g., LinearReg, RandomForest) that are automatically registered in a Model Registry to enable painless model_versioning and shadow deployments. A declarative Pipeline Pattern feeds business data through data_preprocessing, feature_engineering, model_evaluation, and model_monitoring steps. The ViewModel translates business questions—such as “expected weekly demand” or “likelihood of customer churn”—into normalized feature vectors, invokes the selected model, and pushes human-readable results to the View. The View is a thin GTK-based dashboard that offers data_visualization widgets (spark-lines, residual plots) so analysts can explore forecasts without touching the underlying code.

Although the codebase stays ‘easy’ in complexity, it covers all stages of the inference life-cycle a real company meets: automated retraining hooks, JSON-based configuration for A/B testing newer models, and an on-disk audit trail for regulatory compliance. By isolating business logic in the ViewModel and inference mechanics in Model factories, BizSight makes it trivial for non-data-scientist developers to integrate or swap prediction workflows while preserving a clear boundary between UI and analytics.
dependencies: cJSON          (JSON I/O for model_registry metadata & pipeline configs)
OpenBLAS       (matrix ops used by linear models; keeps code pure-C)
cmocka         (unit tests for Model and ViewModel interactions)
